summary.title: Port complexity.combinatorial onto the v3 rule contract
summary.what: Added CombinatorialRule (complexity.combinatorial) — NPath complexity (Nejmeh 1988) at the Callable altitude, threshold NPath>400, ERROR severity, metric via the already-live Structure.over(c).combinatorial(). Completes the cyclomatic/cognitive/combinatorial complexity triad. Registered in RULE_REGISTRY; added tests/test_rule_combinatorial.py. Suite 75->79 green.
summary.why: Second structural rule-only port, continuing to exercise the proven 3-touch workflow. Combinatorial is the direct sibling of the two complexity rules already ported, so the class-gate re-examination was already settled — a low-risk, high-coherence unit.

decisions.point: Keep or drop the legacy class-scope NPath gate?
decisions.rationale: Same complexity-family decision as cyclomatic and cognitive. The class aggregate (sum of method NPaths) was self-described in the legacy as 'slop calibration, no published threshold' — the weakest justification of the three — and is dominated by method count (breadth, not tangle). Nejmeh defined NPath at function scope. The aggregate stays on Structure.combinatorial for any consumer; it is simply not gated.
rejected: Preserve the legacy class-scope gate (sum-of-method-NPath > 1600): reintroduces the breadth-vs-tangle conflation already rejected twice in this family, on the weakest evidence of the three.

decisions.rationale: Preserve the shipped calibration. Nejmeh 1988 recommended 200; slop's default doubled it for agent-generated code where the academic limit floods. Kept the project's calibrated value, documented its origin in the rule docstring.
rejected: Nejmeh's published 200: too noisy on agent-generated code per the existing slop calibration.

rejected.alternative: Batch multiple structural ports in one intent
rejected.reason: Each remaining rule (redundancy, escape_hatches, runts, ...) needs its own re-examination decision; only combinatorial shared the already-settled complexity-family decision, so it was the one clean batch-free unit.
